# PacBio assembly -- findings report

**Generated:** 2026-08-05  ·  auto-generated by `scripts/utils/report_pacbio_assembly.sh`

All figures are in **reference coordinates**, read from the mask BED and the VCF
rather than from the consensus FASTA (the consensus has indels applied, so its
own coordinates drift from the reference).

The distinction this report exists to preserve:

- **unsequenced** -- no read spans the position. Masked to `N`. Nothing can be
  concluded about it, in either direction.
- **deleted** -- reads span the position and agree the base is absent. A called
  variant, not an `N`. This is a positive finding.

A motif that is absent over an unsequenced stretch is **not evidence of absence**.

### Sequenced regions (amplicon structure)

Reads clustered by span endpoints (both ends agreeing within 50bp), NOT merged
by overlap. Reads that stack into a few discrete intervals rather than
tiling the reference indicate an amplicon library, which is what makes
overlap-based de novo assembly structurally impossible for some samples.

| sample | distinct regions | regions (reference coords, read count) |
|---|---|---|
| 124_4 | 3 | 814-8002 (x9); 1963-9719 (x7); 8986-9719 (x24) |
| 128_5 | 3 | 1594-3333 (x1); 1594-7030 (x73); 2340-7030 (x1) |
| 203_3 | 2 | 27-1106 (x10); 27-1193 (x9) |
| 211_0 | 2 | 26-5120 (x21); 4410-6001 (x9) |

### Masking audit

The mask must contain only stretches no read reaches. An **interior** masked
interval -- one with sequenced bases on both sides -- means a position that
reads do span was labelled unsequenced. That regression previously turned
unanimous deletions into `N`, so it is checked on every run.

| sample | mask intervals | interior intervals | interior bp | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 124_4 | 1 | 0 | 0 | OK |
| 128_5 | 2 | 0 | 0 | OK |
| 203_3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | OK |
| 211_0 | 2 | 0 | 0 | OK |

### U3 coverage (the regions of interest)

U3 windows taken from HXB2 annotation in `data/reference/K03455.1.gb`:
5' U3 = 1-453, 3' U3 = 9086-9539 (1-based inclusive).

Both LTRs are identical in an integrated provirus, so **either** copy is a
valid U3 source -- but an amplicon library may only reach one of them.

Windows are HXB2 coordinates, and are only reported for samples mapped against
HXB2. U3 position varies between subtypes (Mbondji-Wonje 2018 reports up to 25%
inter-strain dissimilarity in U3 while R stays conserved), and no per-subtype
coordinate system exists to substitute, so a window projected onto a non-HXB2
reference would be meaningless. Subtype-aware U3 boundaries come from the
alignment-anchored liftover downstream, not from this table.

| sample | 5' U3 sequenced | 3' U3 sequenced | del called in 5' | del called in 3' | usable copy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 124_4 | 0/453 bp (0%) | 454/454 bp (100%) | 0 | 2 | 3' copy |
| 128_5 | 0/453 bp (0%) | 0/454 bp (0%) | 0 | 0 | **neither -- exclude from motif analysis** |
| 203_3 | 427/453 bp (94%) | 0/454 bp (0%) | 3 | 0 | 5' copy |
| 211_0 | 428/453 bp (94%) | 0/454 bp (0%) | 2 | 0 | 5' copy |

## Does subtype-matching reduce divergence?

Total called variants against each arm reference. Fewer variants means the
reference is closer to the sample, so less of the consensus is inherited from
a reference backbone.

| sample | minimap2_consensus (ref, SNV+indel) | minimap2_bestref (ref, SNV+indel) |
|---|---|---|
| 124_4 | HXB2: 965 | D:KU168271: 972 |
| 128_5 | HXB2: 555 | B:K03455: 555 |
| 203_3 | HXB2: 162 | A1:KU168256: 95 |
| 211_0 | HXB2: 609 | D:KU168271: 622 |

- `minimap2_bestref`/128_5: **no U3 sequence at either LTR.** Any motif result for this
